title: Human Health and Body Systems
unitGoal: Students will learn how major body systems work together and how wise habits support health, safety, and care for the body.

lessons.title: Body Systems Work Together
lessons.learningGoal: Students will identify major body systems and explain how systems work together to keep the body alive and active.
successCriteria: I can name major body systems and describe their jobs.
I can explain how two or more systems work together.
I can use evidence from a scenario to decide which systems are involved.
lessons.teacherSummary: Students practise identifying body systems and explaining how systems interact.
lessons.teacherOverview: Students learn that organs and body systems have different jobs, but they work together as one body.
lessons.christianFocus: The human body is wonderfully made by God. Students should study it with care, gratitude, and respect.
lessonContent: A body system is a group of organs and tissues that work together to do an important job.
Major body systems include the digestive, respiratory, circulatory, skeletal, muscular, nervous, and excretory systems.
No body system works completely by itself. Systems interact so the whole body can function.
Cells need oxygen, nutrients, water, and waste removal to keep working.
When one system has trouble, other systems may also be affected.

studentActivity.title: Body Systems Team Mission
studentActivity.mission: Practise matching body systems to their jobs and connections.

steps.title: Before You Begin
steps.prompt: Get ready: the body works as one
steps.text: Your body is made of many parts with different jobs. A body system is a group of organs and tissues that work together. The systems are different, but they are connected.

steps.title: Know the Main Jobs
steps.prompt: Each system has a role
steps.text: The digestive system breaks down food. The respiratory system brings in oxygen. The circulatory system moves materials in the blood. The skeletal and muscular systems help with support and movement. The nervous system sends messages.

steps.title: System Match
steps.prompt: Which system moves oxygen, nutrients, and wastes through the body in the blood?
steps.feedback: Correct. The circulatory system moves blood through the body.
steps.hint: Think about which system includes the heart and blood vessels.

steps.title: Organ Job
steps.prompt: Which statement best describes the lungs?
choices: They help oxygen enter the body and carbon dioxide leave.
They pump blood to body cells.
They break food into smaller nutrient pieces.
steps.correctAnswer: They help oxygen enter the body and carbon dioxide leave.
steps.feedback: Yes. The lungs are part of the respiratory system.
steps.hint: The lungs are linked to breathing.

steps.title: Support and Movement
steps.prompt: Which two systems work most directly when you raise your hand?
steps.feedback: Correct. Bones support the arm, and muscles move it.
steps.hint: Movement usually needs bones and muscles.

steps.title: True or False
steps.prompt: Body systems have separate jobs, but they also depend on each other.
steps.feedback: Correct. The systems are connected.
steps.hint: Different jobs can still work together.

steps.title: Level 1 Complete
steps.prompt: You practised body system jobs.

steps.title: Connections Matter
steps.prompt: Cells need several systems
steps.text: Body cells need oxygen and nutrients. They also need wastes carried away. This means the respiratory, digestive, circulatory, and excretory systems all support cells in different ways.

steps.title: Oxygen Path
steps.prompt: A student breathes in before running. Which systems work together to bring oxygen to leg muscles?
steps.feedback: Correct. The lungs take in oxygen, and blood carries it.
steps.hint: Oxygen enters through breathing and travels in blood.

steps.title: Food to Energy
steps.prompt: After lunch, nutrients from food are absorbed and carried to cells. Which systems are most involved?
steps.feedback: Yes. Digestion breaks down food, and blood carries nutrients.
steps.hint: Think about food first, then transport.

steps.title: Body Response
steps.prompt: A student touches a warm mug and pulls a hand away. Which system quickly sends the message?
steps.feedback: Correct. The nervous system sends fast messages.
steps.hint: This is about sensing and responding.

steps.title: True or False
steps.prompt: A healthy body needs systems to interact, not just do separate jobs.
steps.feedback: Correct. Interaction keeps the body functioning.
steps.hint: The whole body works together.

steps.title: Mission Complete
steps.prompt: You practised explaining body system connections.

questions.prompt: Which system moves materials through the body in blood?
questions.reviewNote: The circulatory system includes the heart, blood, and blood vessels.

questions.prompt: Which organ helps oxygen enter the body?
questions.reviewNote: The lungs are part of the respiratory system.

questions.prompt: Which systems work together most directly when a student walks across the room?
questions.reviewNote: Bones and muscles work together for movement.

questions.prompt: Why do body systems need to interact?
choices: Cells need oxygen, nutrients, messages, support, and waste removal.
Each system can do every body job by itself.
Organs change systems whenever the body is active.
questions.correctAnswer: Cells need oxygen, nutrients, messages, support, and waste removal.
questions.reviewNote: Different systems meet different body needs.

questions.prompt: A runner breathes faster and the heart beats faster. Which systems are clearly working together?
questions.reviewNote: Breathing brings oxygen in, and blood moves it.

questions.prompt: Which system sends messages between the brain and body?
questions.reviewNote: The nervous system sends and receives messages.

questions.prompt: Organs in a body system work together to do a job.
questions.reviewNote: A body system is made of working parts.

questions.prompt: The digestive system and circulatory system can both be involved after a meal.
questions.reviewNote: Digestion breaks down food, and blood carries nutrients.

lessons.title: Digestion and Nutrients
lessons.learningGoal: Students will describe how digestion breaks food into nutrients and how nutrients support body cells.
successCriteria: I can explain the main job of digestion.
I can identify how nutrients help the body.
I can connect digestion to energy, growth, repair, and body care.
lessons.teacherSummary: Students practise understanding digestion, nutrients, and healthy food choices without personal food tracking.
lessons.teacherOverview: Students learn that digestion breaks down food and that nutrients support body energy, growth, and repair.
lessons.christianFocus: Food is part of God's provision. Students can learn wise habits without judging people by what they eat.
lessonContent: Digestion breaks food into smaller parts that the body can use.
Nutrients include carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, water, and fibre.
Different nutrients support different needs such as energy, growth, repair, and healthy body processes.
The small intestine absorbs many nutrients into the blood.
Wise food choices over time can support health, but one snack or meal does not tell a person's whole health story.

studentActivity.title: Digestion and Nutrients Mission
studentActivity.mission: Practise explaining how food is broken down and used by the body.

steps.title: Before You Begin
steps.prompt: Get ready: food must be broken down
steps.text: Food cannot help body cells until it is broken into usable parts. Digestion uses chewing, stomach mixing, and chemical changes to break food down.

steps.title: From Food to Nutrients
steps.prompt: Absorption matters
steps.text: After food is broken down, many nutrients are absorbed through the small intestine into the blood. Then the circulatory system carries them where they are needed.

steps.title: Main Job
steps.prompt: What is the main job of the digestive system?
choices: break food into parts the body can use
move oxygen from the lungs to cells
send messages from the brain to muscles
steps.correctAnswer: break food into parts the body can use
steps.feedback: Correct. Digestion breaks food into usable parts.
steps.hint: Think about what happens to food.

steps.title: Organ Role
steps.prompt: Which organ mixes food with digestive juices after it is swallowed?
steps.feedback: Yes. The stomach mixes food during digestion.
steps.hint: Food goes to this organ after the esophagus.

steps.title: Absorption
steps.prompt: Why is the small intestine important?
choices: Many nutrients are absorbed there into the blood.
It protects the brain from injury.
steps.correctAnswer: Many nutrients are absorbed there into the blood.
steps.feedback: Correct. Absorption is a key job of the small intestine.
steps.hint: Think about nutrients entering the blood.

steps.title: True or False
steps.prompt: Digestion and circulation can work together after a meal.
steps.feedback: Correct. Digestion breaks food down, and blood carries nutrients.
steps.hint: Food and transport connect.

steps.title: Level 1 Complete
steps.prompt: You practised digestion jobs.

steps.title: Different Nutrients Help Different Ways
steps.prompt: The body needs variety
steps.text: Nutrients do different jobs. Carbohydrates can provide energy. Protein helps growth and repair. Vitamins and minerals support body processes. Water helps many body systems work.

steps.title: Energy
steps.prompt: Which nutrient group is often a main source of quick energy for the body?
steps.feedback: Correct. Carbohydrates often provide energy.
steps.hint: Bread, rice, fruit, and potatoes contain carbohydrates.

steps.title: Growth and Repair
steps.prompt: Why does the body need protein?
choices: to help build and repair body tissues
to replace the job of drinking water
to make bones bend like muscles
steps.correctAnswer: to help build and repair body tissues
steps.feedback: Yes. Protein supports growth and repair.
steps.hint: Think about building and fixing tissues.

steps.title: Fibre
steps.prompt: Which choice best explains fibre?
choices: It helps food move through the digestive system.
It carries oxygen in red blood cells.
It sends nerve messages from the spinal cord.
steps.correctAnswer: It helps food move through the digestive system.
steps.feedback: Correct. Fibre supports digestion.
steps.hint: Fibre is connected to digestion.

steps.title: True or False
steps.prompt: A balanced eating pattern includes different kinds of nutrients over time.
steps.feedback: Correct. Variety helps meet body needs.
steps.hint: One food cannot provide every need.

steps.title: Mission Complete
steps.prompt: You practised connecting nutrients to body needs.

questions.prompt: What does digestion do?
questions.reviewNote: Digestion helps the body use food.

questions.prompt: Which organ mixes food after it is swallowed?
questions.reviewNote: The stomach mixes food with digestive juices.

questions.prompt: Why is the small intestine important?
choices: It absorbs many nutrients into the blood.
questions.correctAnswer: It absorbs many nutrients into the blood.
questions.reviewNote: Many nutrients enter the blood there.

questions.prompt: Which nutrient group often gives the body energy?
questions.reviewNote: Carbohydrates are a common energy source.

questions.prompt: Protein helps the body mainly by...
questions.reviewNote: Protein helps build and repair tissues.

questions.prompt: Why does the body need water?
choices: Many body processes depend on it.
It becomes oxygen in the lungs.
questions.correctAnswer: Many body processes depend on it.

questions.prompt: The digestive and circulatory systems work together when nutrients enter the blood.
One food choice tells everything about a person's health.
questions.reviewNote: Health is supported by many habits over time.

lessons.title: Breathing, Blood, and the Heart
lessons.learningGoal: Students will explain how the respiratory and circulatory systems work together to move oxygen and carbon dioxide.
successCriteria: I can describe the job of the respiratory system.
I can describe the job of the heart, blood, and blood vessels.
I can explain how oxygen and carbon dioxide move through the body.
lessons.teacherSummary: Students practise connecting breathing, blood flow, oxygen movement, and carbon dioxide removal.
lessons.teacherOverview: Students learn how the lungs, heart, blood, and blood vessels work together to support cells.
lessons.christianFocus: Breathing and heartbeat remind students that life is a precious gift and the body should be treated with care.
lessonContent: The respiratory system brings oxygen into the body and removes carbon dioxide.
The lungs are the main organs of the respiratory system.
The circulatory system includes the heart, blood, and blood vessels.
Blood carries oxygen and nutrients to cells and carries wastes away.
During exercise, breathing and heart rate may increase because cells need more oxygen and produce more carbon dioxide.

studentActivity.title: Oxygen Delivery Mission
studentActivity.mission: Practise tracing how breathing and blood flow help body cells.

steps.title: Before You Begin
steps.prompt: Get ready: oxygen has a path
steps.text: When you breathe in, oxygen enters the lungs. From there, oxygen moves into the blood. The heart pumps blood so oxygen can reach body cells.

steps.title: Carbon Dioxide Leaves
steps.prompt: The path works both ways
steps.text: Cells use oxygen and give off carbon dioxide. Blood carries carbon dioxide back to the lungs, and the respiratory system removes it when you breathe out.

steps.title: Respiratory Job
steps.prompt: What is one main job of the respiratory system?
steps.feedback: Correct. Breathing brings oxygen into the body.
steps.hint: The respiratory system is linked to lungs and breathing.

steps.title: Circulatory Job
steps.prompt: What is one main job of the circulatory system?
steps.feedback: Yes. The heart pumps blood through blood vessels.
steps.hint: Think about the heart and blood.

steps.title: Oxygen Delivery
steps.prompt: Which order best shows oxygen reaching body cells?
steps.feedback: Correct. Oxygen enters at the lungs and travels in blood.
steps.hint: Start with breathing in.

steps.title: True or False
steps.prompt: Blood can carry both useful materials and wastes.
steps.feedback: Correct. Blood carries oxygen and nutrients, and it helps carry wastes away.
steps.hint: Blood is a transport system.

steps.title: Level 1 Complete
steps.prompt: You practised breathing and blood flow.

steps.title: Activity Changes Demand
steps.prompt: Cells need more during movement
steps.text: When muscles work harder, they need more oxygen and nutrients. They also produce more carbon dioxide. Breathing and heart rate often change to meet that need.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.prompt: Why might breathing become faster during a long run?
choices: Working muscles need more oxygen and must get rid of more carbon dioxide.
The stomach needs extra time to absorb fibre.
Bones need to make new blood vessels quickly.
steps.correctAnswer: Working muscles need more oxygen and must get rid of more carbon dioxide.
steps.feedback: Correct. Breathing changes when cells need more gas exchange.
steps.hint: Think about active muscles.

steps.title: Heart Rate
steps.prompt: Why might the heart beat faster during exercise?
choices: to move blood more quickly to and from active muscles
to make air enter the stomach more quickly
to stop bones from bending at joints
steps.correctAnswer: to move blood more quickly to and from active muscles
steps.feedback: Yes. Faster blood flow can help meet increased needs.
steps.hint: The heart pumps blood.

steps.title: Carbon Dioxide
steps.prompt: What happens to carbon dioxide made by body cells?
choices: Blood carries it to the lungs so it can be breathed out.
The stomach changes it into nutrients.
Bones store it until the body rests.
steps.correctAnswer: Blood carries it to the lungs so it can be breathed out.
steps.feedback: Correct. Carbon dioxide is removed through breathing.
steps.hint: Carbon dioxide leaves through the lungs.

steps.title: True or False
steps.prompt: Respiratory and circulatory systems work together to support active muscles.
steps.feedback: Correct. Breathing and blood flow work together.
steps.hint: Oxygen enters through breathing and travels in blood.

steps.title: Mission Complete
steps.prompt: You practised connecting breathing, blood, and body needs.

quiz.title: Breathing, Blood, and the Heart Quiz

questions.prompt: What does the respiratory system do?
choices: brings in oxygen and removes carbon dioxide
questions.correctAnswer: brings in oxygen and removes carbon dioxide
questions.reviewNote: That is the gas exchange job.

questions.prompt: Which organs are central to breathing?
questions.reviewNote: The lungs are part of the respiratory system.

questions.prompt: What does the heart do?
What does blood carry to body cells?
How does carbon dioxide leave the body?
choices: It is carried to the lungs and breathed out.
It is stored in the stomach.
questions.correctAnswer: It is carried to the lungs and breathed out.

questions.prompt: Why can heart rate increase during exercise?
choices: Active muscles need materials moved more quickly.
The digestive system stops needing nutrients.
The nervous system turns into a muscle.
questions.correctAnswer: Active muscles need materials moved more quickly.

questions.prompt: The respiratory and circulatory systems work together.
questions.reviewNote: Oxygen enters through lungs and travels in blood.

questions.prompt: Carbon dioxide is a waste gas made by cells.

lessons.title: Bones, Muscles, and Nerves
lessons.learningGoal: Students will explain how the skeletal, muscular, and nervous systems support movement, protection, and response.
successCriteria: I can describe jobs of bones, muscles, and nerves.
I can explain how muscles and bones work together at joints.
I can use a scenario to identify nervous system messages.
lessons.teacherSummary: Students practise connecting bones, muscles, joints, nerves, and body responses.
lessons.teacherOverview: Students learn how the skeletal, muscular, and nervous systems work together for support, movement, protection, and response.
lessons.christianFocus: Students study the body's design with respect and care, recognizing that each person should be treated with dignity.
lessonContent: The skeletal system supports the body and protects important organs.
Muscles pull on bones to create movement.
Joints are places where bones meet and movement can happen.
The nervous system includes the brain, spinal cord, and nerves.
Nerves carry messages that help the body sense, decide, and respond.

lessons.assessmentPlan: Use the activity to build confidence and the quiz to check independent understanding.

studentActivity.title: Movement and Messages Mission
studentActivity.mission: Practise explaining how bones, muscles, joints, and nerves work together.

steps.title: Before You Begin
steps.prompt: Get ready: movement needs teamwork
steps.text: Your skeleton gives support and shape. Muscles pull on bones to move body parts. Joints allow many movements to happen in controlled ways.

steps.title: Bones Protect
steps.prompt: Support is not the only job
steps.text: Some bones protect important organs. The skull protects the brain, and the ribs help protect the heart and lungs.

steps.title: Skeleton Job
steps.prompt: Which statement best describes one job of the skeletal system?
choices: It supports the body and protects some organs.
It breaks food into nutrients in the stomach.
It carries oxygen into the lungs.
steps.correctAnswer: It supports the body and protects some organs.
steps.feedback: Correct. Support and protection are skeletal system jobs.
steps.hint: Think about bones.

steps.title: Muscle Job
steps.prompt: How do muscles help the body move?
choices: They pull on bones at joints.
steps.correctAnswer: They pull on bones at joints.
steps.feedback: Yes. Muscles pull to create movement.
steps.hint: Muscles and bones work together.

steps.title: Protection
steps.prompt: Which body part is protected by the skull?
steps.feedback: Correct. The skull protects the brain.
steps.hint: The skull is the bone structure around the head.

steps.title: True or False
steps.prompt: A joint is a place where two bones meet.
steps.feedback: Correct. Joints are places where bones meet.
steps.hint: Joints help movement happen.

steps.title: Level 1 Complete
steps.prompt: You practised support, protection, and movement.

steps.title: Nerves Carry Messages
steps.prompt: The body senses and responds
steps.text: The nervous system sends messages between the brain, spinal cord, and body. These messages help you notice your surroundings, move, and respond.

steps.title: Nervous System
steps.prompt: Which parts belong to the nervous system?
choices: stomach, small intestine, and large intestine
steps.feedback: Correct. These parts send and receive messages.
steps.hint: Think about messages and control.

steps.title: Fast Response
steps.prompt: A student touches a hot pan handle and pulls the hand away quickly. Which system helps with this quick response?
steps.feedback: Yes. The nervous system helps the body respond quickly.
steps.hint: This scenario is about sensing heat and responding.

steps.title: Coordinated Movement
steps.prompt: Which systems work together when a student catches a ball?
steps.feedback: Correct. The body senses, decides, and moves.
steps.hint: Catching needs messages and movement.

steps.title: True or False
steps.prompt: The nervous system helps the body respond to information from the senses.
steps.feedback: Correct. Senses send information through the nervous system.
steps.hint: The body responds to messages.

steps.title: Mission Complete
steps.prompt: You practised movement and nervous system responses.

questions.prompt: Which is a job of the skeletal system?
choices: supporting the body and protecting organs
questions.correctAnswer: supporting the body and protecting organs

questions.prompt: How do muscles move body parts?
What is a joint?
What does the skull protect?
Which parts belong to the nervous system?
A student hears a whistle and stops running. Which system helps process the sound and response?
questions.reviewNote: The nervous system helps sense and respond.

questions.prompt: Bones and muscles work together during movement.
The nervous system sends messages that help the body respond.

lessons.title: Healthy Habits and Body Care
lessons.learningGoal: Students will connect wise health habits with body systems while respecting privacy and individual needs.
successCriteria: I can explain how sleep, movement, nutrition, hygiene, and hydration support body systems.
I can choose general health advice that is safe and respectful.
I can avoid judging a person by one habit, meal, or moment.
lessons.teacherSummary: Students practise general health-habit reasoning without personal health disclosure.
lessons.teacherOverview: Students learn how general healthy habits support the body while avoiding private personal sharing or judging others.
lessons.christianFocus: The body is a gift from God. Students can learn wise care while showing kindness and respect to every person.
lessonContent: Healthy habits can support many body systems over time.
Sleep helps the body rest, grow, repair, learn, and focus.
Movement strengthens muscles, bones, heart, lungs, and coordination.
Hygiene habits, such as handwashing, help reduce the spread of germs.
Health advice should be general, respectful, and safe. Private health questions should go to a parent, guardian, teacher, or health professional.

studentActivity.title: Body Care Choices Mission
studentActivity.mission: Practise choosing general habits that support body systems wisely and respectfully.

steps.title: Before You Begin
steps.prompt: Get ready: habits support systems
steps.text: Healthy habits do not make every person the same, but they can support the body over time. Sleep, movement, water, nutrition, and hygiene can help several systems work well.

steps.title: Think Generally
steps.prompt: No private sharing needed
steps.text: This lesson uses general science examples. Students do not need to share private health details, family routines, medical information, or personal food records.

steps.title: Sleep
steps.prompt: Why is sleep important for the body?
choices: It supports rest, growth, repair, learning, and focus.
It replaces the need for food and water.
It makes the digestive system do every body job.
steps.correctAnswer: It supports rest, growth, repair, learning, and focus.
steps.feedback: Correct. Sleep supports many body needs.
steps.hint: Think about what rest helps the body do.

steps.title: Movement
steps.prompt: Which statement best connects movement to body systems?
choices: Movement can strengthen muscles, bones, heart, lungs, and coordination.
Movement mainly strengthens muscles but has little effect on breathing.
Movement supports bones but does not connect much to coordination.
steps.correctAnswer: Movement can strengthen muscles, bones, heart, lungs, and coordination.
steps.feedback: Yes. Movement can support several systems.
steps.hint: Many systems are involved when the body moves.

steps.title: Hydration
steps.prompt: Why does the body need water?
choices: Water supports many body processes and helps transport materials.
Water keeps the skeleton from needing joints.
steps.correctAnswer: Water supports many body processes and helps transport materials.
steps.feedback: Correct. Water helps many body systems.
steps.hint: Water is used throughout the body.

steps.title: True or False
steps.prompt: Handwashing can help reduce the spread of germs.
steps.feedback: Correct. Handwashing is an important hygiene habit.
steps.hint: Hygiene can help prevent illness.

steps.title: Level 1 Complete
steps.prompt: You practised connecting habits to body systems.

steps.title: Respect People
steps.prompt: Health is not for judging
steps.text: Good health learning should not be used to embarrass or judge people. A student can learn general habits while remembering that families, bodies, medical needs, and circumstances can be different.

steps.title: Respectful Advice
steps.prompt: Which advice is most respectful and useful for a class health poster?
choices: Choose water often and ask a trusted adult if you are unsure about health needs.
Choose a routine that works for one student and use it as the class rule.
Compare meals to decide which student has the healthiest habits.
steps.correctAnswer: Choose water often and ask a trusted adult if you are unsure about health needs.
steps.feedback: Correct. It is general, safe, and respectful.
steps.hint: Look for advice that helps without judging.

steps.title: Privacy
steps.prompt: Which question should not be required for a class science activity?
choices: What private medical condition has your family dealt with?
Which body system helps move oxygen?
What general habit can help reduce germs?
steps.correctAnswer: What private medical condition has your family dealt with?
steps.feedback: Yes. Private medical details should not be required.
steps.hint: Science class can learn without private health sharing.

steps.title: Trusted Help
steps.prompt: A student has a personal health question after a lesson. Which response is best?
choices: Ask a parent, guardian, teacher, or health professional for help.
Compare class notes and decide what the answer must be.
Ask classmates what they think before telling an adult.
steps.correctAnswer: Ask a parent, guardian, teacher, or health professional for help.
steps.feedback: Correct. Personal health questions need trusted help.
steps.hint: Personal health questions need care.

steps.title: True or False
steps.prompt: General health learning should be respectful and should not require private health details.
steps.feedback: Correct. Privacy and respect matter.
steps.hint: Health learning should be safe.

steps.title: Mission Complete
steps.prompt: You practised wise and respectful body-care choices.

quiz.title: Healthy Habits and Body Care Quiz

questions.prompt: Which statement about sleep is most accurate?
choices: Sleep supports rest, learning, growth, and repair.
Sleep replaces oxygen during the day.
Sleep makes bones move without muscles.
questions.correctAnswer: Sleep supports rest, learning, growth, and repair.

questions.prompt: Which systems can movement support?
choices: muscular, skeletal, respiratory, circulatory, and nervous systems
questions.correctAnswer: muscular, skeletal, respiratory, circulatory, and nervous systems
questions.reviewNote: Movement uses and supports several systems.

questions.prompt: Why is water important?
choices: It controls every system by itself.
questions.reviewNote: Water has many roles in the body.

questions.prompt: Why is handwashing useful?
choices: It can reduce the spread of germs.
It replaces sleep when a student is tired.
It makes blood carry less oxygen.
questions.correctAnswer: It can reduce the spread of germs.

questions.prompt: Which health advice is best for a general class poster?
choices: Choose habits that support your body, and ask a trusted adult when unsure.
Every student must follow the same private family routine.
One snack choice shows whether someone is healthy.
questions.correctAnswer: Choose habits that support your body, and ask a trusted adult when unsure.

questions.prompt: Which question is suitable for class science?
choices: Which system helps oxygen travel through the body?
What medicine does your family use?
Which private health concern has affected your home?
questions.correctAnswer: Which system helps oxygen travel through the body?
questions.reviewNote: It checks science understanding without private details.

questions.prompt: Health learning should avoid embarrassing or judging people.
Personal health questions should be handled with trusted adults or health professionals.

lessons.title: Prevention and Wise Choices
lessons.learningGoal: Students will identify prevention habits and wise choices that reduce risk and support body health.
successCriteria: I can explain how prevention habits can reduce risk.
I can choose safe actions in age-appropriate health and safety scenarios.
I can identify when a trusted adult should be involved.
lessons.teacherSummary: Students practise prevention and safety choices, including illness prevention and trusted adult support.
lessons.teacherOverview: Students learn that prevention means taking wise steps before harm or illness happens.
lessons.christianFocus: Wise choices show stewardship of the body God has given and care for neighbours who may be affected by our actions.
lessonContent: Prevention means taking wise steps to reduce risk before a problem happens.
Some prevention habits reduce the spread of germs, such as handwashing and staying home when truly sick.
Safety habits reduce the chance of injury during activity, tools, travel, and experiments.
Trusted adults can help when a situation is confusing, unsafe, or personal.
Wise choices can protect both the person making the choice and other people nearby.

studentActivity.title: Prevention Choices Mission
studentActivity.mission: Practise choosing prevention and safety actions in everyday scenarios.

steps.title: Before You Begin
steps.prompt: Get ready: prevention happens early
steps.text: Prevention means making a wise choice before a problem happens. It does not remove every risk, but it can lower the chance of harm or illness.

steps.title: Care for Others
steps.prompt: Choices can affect people nearby
steps.text: Health and safety choices often affect more than one person. Washing hands, using tools properly, and following safety instructions can help protect a whole group.

steps.title: Germs
steps.prompt: Which action helps reduce the spread of germs before snack time?
choices: wash hands carefully with soap and water
check whether the snack package has a label
move desks so everyone has more space
steps.correctAnswer: wash hands carefully with soap and water
steps.feedback: Correct. Handwashing can reduce germs.
steps.hint: Think about hygiene before eating.

steps.title: Safety Gear
steps.prompt: Why might a helmet be important when cycling?
choices: It helps protect the head if a fall happens.
It makes the bike move with less effort.
It improves how the legs push the pedals.
steps.correctAnswer: It helps protect the head if a fall happens.
steps.feedback: Yes. Safety gear reduces risk.
steps.hint: Think about preventing injury.

steps.title: Science Safety
steps.prompt: A student is not sure whether a material is safe to touch during an investigation. What should the student do?
choices: ask the teacher before handling it
read the label and decide alone
move it with another tool to save time
steps.correctAnswer: ask the teacher before handling it
steps.feedback: Correct. Unknown materials need adult guidance.
steps.hint: Unclear safety instructions require help.

steps.title: True or False
steps.prompt: Prevention means taking wise steps before a problem happens.
steps.feedback: Correct. Prevention happens before the problem when possible.
steps.hint: Prevention is early action.

steps.title: Level 1 Complete
steps.prompt: You practised risk-reducing choices.

steps.title: Trusted Adults Matter
steps.prompt: Some choices need guidance
steps.text: Students do not need to solve every health or safety problem alone. A parent, guardian, teacher, or health professional can help with personal, confusing, or unsafe situations.

steps.title: Personal Health
steps.prompt: A student has a personal question about a symptom that is not part of a class activity. Which choice is best?
choices: talk with a parent, guardian, teacher, or health professional
compare class notes and decide what the symptom means
ask classmates whether they have heard of the symptom
steps.correctAnswer: talk with a parent, guardian, teacher, or health professional
steps.feedback: Correct. Personal health questions need trusted help.
steps.hint: Personal health needs care.

steps.title: Unsafe Situation
steps.prompt: A teammate wants to skip safety instructions during a science task. What is the wisest response?
choices: pause and ask the teacher to review the instructions
continue only with the steps that seem familiar
let the teammate decide because speed is helpful
steps.correctAnswer: pause and ask the teacher to review the instructions
steps.feedback: Yes. Safety is worth pausing for.
steps.hint: Unsafe pressure needs adult support.

steps.title: Careful Information
steps.prompt: Which source is strongest for a personal health question?
choices: a trusted adult or health professional
a comment from an unknown person online
a short video that does not name its source
steps.correctAnswer: a trusted adult or health professional
steps.feedback: Correct. Personal health questions need reliable guidance.
steps.hint: Think about safety and reliability.

steps.title: True or False
steps.prompt: Asking for help can be a wise prevention choice.
steps.feedback: Correct. Help can prevent unsafe choices.
steps.hint: Help is part of safety.

steps.title: Mission Complete
steps.prompt: You practised prevention and trusted-help choices.

questions.prompt: What does prevention mean?
choices: taking wise steps before a problem happens
waiting until every risk is gone
choosing the fastest option in a task
questions.correctAnswer: taking wise steps before a problem happens

questions.prompt: Which action can reduce the spread of germs?
choices: checking a food label before eating
wiping crumbs from a desk after eating

questions.prompt: Why use a helmet for cycling?
choices: to help protect the head during a fall
to make the bicycle easier to steer
to help the lungs take in more oxygen
questions.correctAnswer: to help protect the head during a fall
questions.reviewNote: A helmet helps reduce injury risk.

questions.prompt: What should a student do if a science instruction is unclear?
choices: try the step and see what happens
skip the safety part of the task

questions.prompt: Who should help with a personal health question?
choices: a parent, guardian, teacher, or health professional
a website comment from someone not known to the student
a classmate who once had a similar question
questions.correctAnswer: a parent, guardian, teacher, or health professional
questions.reviewNote: Personal health questions need trusted help.

questions.prompt: A group wants to rush through a safety step. What is the best choice?
choices: pause and check with the teacher
rush only if the materials look familiar
questions.correctAnswer: pause and check with the teacher

questions.prompt: Prevention choices can help protect other people too.
questions.reviewNote: Many safety and health choices affect others.

questions.prompt: A careful student can ask for help when a situation feels unsafe or confusing.

lessons.title: Body Systems Case Studies
lessons.learningGoal: Students will use body-system evidence to reason through simple health and activity scenarios.
successCriteria: I can identify which systems are involved in a scenario.
I can explain a body-system connection using evidence.
I can choose a wise next step when a scenario includes safety or health concerns.
lessons.teacherSummary: Students practise applying body-system knowledge to case studies and health technology scenarios.
lessons.teacherOverview: Students use age-appropriate scenarios to reason about interacting body systems, evidence, and wise choices.
lessons.christianFocus: Students learn to apply knowledge with humility, care for the body, and respect for people who may need support or medical technology.
lessonContent: A case study is a short scenario used for careful thinking.
Body-system case studies ask which systems are involved and what evidence supports the answer.
Health technologies can help people observe, protect, or support body systems.
A good explanation connects the scenario details to body-system jobs.
Some scenarios need a trusted adult or health professional instead of a student guess.
practiceIdeas: Share the student mission for practice stars.
Use the lesson quiz as the scored check.
Review missed ideas before assigning the next Human Health and Body Systems lesson.

studentActivityPlan.title: Body Systems Case Mission
studentActivityPlan.description: Practise using evidence to explain body-system scenarios.
studentActivityPlan.reward: 10 practice stars after each completed level

quizPlan.title: Body Systems Case Studies Quiz
quizPlan.format: Multiple choice and true/false questions with one score at the end.
quizPlan.focus: Scenario evidence, interacting systems, activity changes, health technology, and wise next steps

lessons.assessmentPlan: Use the activity to build confidence and the quiz to check independent understanding.

studentActivity.title: Body Systems Case Mission
studentActivity.mission: Practise using evidence to explain body-system scenarios.

steps.title: Before You Begin
steps.prompt: Get ready: use clues from the case
steps.text: A body-system case study gives clues. Look for breathing, blood flow, movement, digestion, messages, support, waste removal, or safety needs.

steps.title: Evidence First
steps.prompt: Do not guess from one word
steps.text: A careful explanation uses details from the scenario. If a student is running, the muscular system may be involved, but breathing and blood flow may also matter.

steps.title: Running Scenario
steps.prompt: During a relay, a student's breathing and heart rate increase. Which systems are most clearly involved?
steps.feedback: Correct. The scenario mentions breathing and heart rate.
steps.hint: Use the clues in the sentence.

steps.title: Lunch Scenario
steps.prompt: After lunch, nutrients from food are carried through the blood. Which systems are most clearly connected?
steps.feedback: Yes. Food is digested, and nutrients travel in blood.
steps.hint: Food plus blood gives the clue.

steps.title: Reaction Scenario
steps.prompt: A student hears the teacher's signal and stops moving. Which systems work together?
steps.feedback: Correct. The student senses a signal and changes movement.
steps.hint: Sensing and movement are both involved.

steps.title: True or False
steps.prompt: A scenario can involve more than one body system at the same time.
steps.feedback: Correct. Many body activities need several systems.
steps.hint: Body systems interact.

steps.title: Level 1 Complete
steps.prompt: You practised identifying systems in scenarios.

steps.title: Explain With Evidence
steps.prompt: Show your thinking
steps.text: A strong answer says which systems are involved and why. If a scenario includes an injury, illness, or personal health concern, the wise next step may involve a trusted adult.

steps.title: Evidence Explanation
steps.prompt: Which explanation best fits this case: A student climbs stairs and begins breathing faster.
choices: Muscles need more oxygen, so breathing and blood flow help meet the need.
The stomach is absorbing more fibre, so the lungs slow down.
Bones begin pumping blood, so breathing becomes less important.
steps.correctAnswer: Muscles need more oxygen, so breathing and blood flow help meet the need.
steps.feedback: Correct. It connects movement to oxygen needs.
steps.hint: Look for systems connected by evidence.

steps.title: Health Technology
steps.prompt: Why might a thermometer be useful during a health concern?
choices: It measures body temperature, which can be useful information for a trusted adult.
It tells which nutrients are in a meal.
It shows how fast blood is moving through every vessel.
steps.correctAnswer: It measures body temperature, which can be useful information for a trusted adult.
steps.feedback: Yes. A thermometer gives information that can help decision-making.
steps.hint: Think about what the tool actually measures.

steps.title: Wise Next Step
steps.prompt: A student feels unwell during class and is unsure what to do. Which next step is best?
choices: tell the teacher or another trusted adult
wait until the end of class before deciding what to do
compare symptoms with classmates before asking for help
steps.correctAnswer: tell the teacher or another trusted adult
steps.feedback: Correct. Personal health concerns need trusted help.
steps.hint: Students should not handle personal health concerns alone.

steps.title: True or False
steps.prompt: A good body-system explanation should connect evidence from the case to the system's job.
steps.feedback: Correct. Evidence supports the explanation.
steps.hint: Explain why the system fits.

steps.title: Mission Complete
steps.prompt: You practised explaining body-system case studies.

questions.prompt: A student runs across the playground and breathes faster. Which systems are clearly involved?
questions.reviewNote: Running uses muscles and increases oxygen needs.

questions.prompt: Nutrients from lunch enter the blood and travel to cells. Which systems are connected?
questions.reviewNote: Digestion and blood transport are connected.

questions.prompt: A student sees a ball coming and moves hands to catch it. Which systems are involved?
questions.reviewNote: Seeing, deciding, and moving are involved.

questions.prompt: Which explanation uses evidence well?
choices: The heart and lungs are involved because the case mentions faster heartbeat and breathing.
The stomach is involved because all activities use energy.
The skeleton is involved because the student is in Grade 5.
questions.correctAnswer: The heart and lungs are involved because the case mentions faster heartbeat and breathing.

questions.prompt: What does a thermometer measure?
What should a student do with a personal health concern at school?
choices: tell a teacher or trusted adult
keep guessing until it goes away
questions.correctAnswer: tell a teacher or trusted adult

questions.prompt: A case study can involve several body systems.
Evidence from the scenario should support the body-system explanation.

lessons.title: Unit 2 Final Quiz
lessons.teacherSummary: The Unit 2 final quiz checks body systems, digestion, nutrients, breathing, blood flow, movement, healthy habits, prevention, trusted adults, and case-study reasoning.
lessons.teacherOverview: Use this quiz after students complete the Human Health and Body Systems lessons.

quiz.title: Human Health and Body Systems Unit Quiz

questions.prompt: Which system moves blood through the body?
Why do body systems need to work together?
choices: Cells need oxygen, nutrients, messages, support, and waste removal.
Most systems do similar jobs and can switch roles when needed.
Organs usually work best when systems stay separate.
questions.correctAnswer: Cells need oxygen, nutrients, messages, support, and waste removal.

questions.prompt: What is the main job of the digestive system?
choices: break food into parts the body can use
send messages between brain and body
questions.correctAnswer: break food into parts the body can use

questions.prompt: Why is the small intestine important?
choices: Many nutrients are absorbed there into the blood.
It protects the brain from injury.
It helps air move into the lungs.
questions.correctAnswer: Many nutrients are absorbed there into the blood.
questions.reviewNote: Absorption is a key job of the small intestine.

questions.prompt: Which nutrient job is connected to protein?
What does the respiratory system do?
choices: brings in oxygen and removes carbon dioxide
questions.correctAnswer: brings in oxygen and removes carbon dioxide

questions.prompt: Which path best shows oxygen reaching cells?
questions.reviewNote: Oxygen enters through lungs and travels in blood.

questions.prompt: Why can heart rate increase during exercise?
choices: Active muscles need materials moved more quickly.
The stomach stops digesting all food.
The skeleton begins carrying oxygen by itself.
questions.correctAnswer: Active muscles need materials moved more quickly.

questions.prompt: Which is a job of the skeletal system?
choices: supporting the body and protecting organs
questions.correctAnswer: supporting the body and protecting organs

questions.prompt: How do muscles help body parts move?
choices: They pull on bones at joints.
They carry carbon dioxide out of the body.
questions.correctAnswer: They pull on bones at joints.

questions.prompt: Which system sends messages between the brain and body?
Which statement about sleep is most accurate?
choices: Sleep supports rest, growth, repair, learning, and focus.
Sleep makes every body system stop working.
questions.correctAnswer: Sleep supports rest, growth, repair, learning, and focus.
questions.reviewNote: Sleep supports the body in many ways.

questions.prompt: Which statement about movement is most accurate?
choices: Movement can support muscles, bones, heart, lungs, and coordination.
Movement only affects one body system.
Movement prevents the body from needing rest.
questions.correctAnswer: Movement can support muscles, bones, heart, lungs, and coordination.

questions.prompt: Which question is suitable for a class science activity?
choices: Which system carries oxygen in blood?
What private health condition has your family faced?
What medicine does someone in your home use?
questions.correctAnswer: Which system carries oxygen in blood?
questions.reviewNote: It checks science without private sharing.

questions.prompt: What does prevention mean?
choices: taking wise steps before a problem happens
waiting until a problem has become worse
choosing a faster option instead of a safer one
questions.correctAnswer: taking wise steps before a problem happens

questions.prompt: What should a student do if science safety instructions are unclear?
choices: continue with the parts that seem familiar
let a classmate decide the next step

questions.prompt: A student hears a signal and moves to stop. Which systems are clearly involved?
questions.reviewNote: The student senses, decides, and moves.

questions.prompt: What does a thermometer measure?
Body systems often work together during one activity.
A personal health concern should be handled with help from a trusted adult or health professional.
questions.reviewNote: Personal health concerns need trusted help.
